{{Quote|The scale of the Imperial war machine is unprecedented. Never before in the history of the galaxy has such a fighting force been assembled. Never in such numbers, never with so much variety, and never on so many worlds. There is little in the galaxy that is not under the Empire's control, and it is but a trivial act for the Empire to annex a new world when the Emperor wills it.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''|<ref name="Commander's Guide" />}}
The '''Imperial Military''', also known as the '''Imperial Armed Forces''' or '''Imperial Service''', was the armed forces of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and successor to the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]]. It was responsible for carrying out military operations throughout the galaxy as well as maintaining order on Imperial member worlds, governorships, colonies, and protectorates.

The Imperial Military was a massive organization, as Palpatine did nothing to halt the massive military build up that had produced an army of troopers and enormous weapons of mass destruction following the Clone Wars.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> At the height of the Empire's reign, it's military ranks were filled with tens of trillions of regular army soldiers, trillions of fleet crew, and a sizable force of stormtroopers.<ref name="Rebellion Era Campaign Guide">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

The Imperial Military was under the direct control of [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]]. Although the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] acted as the [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|Commander-in-Chief]] of the Military, Palpatine rarely ever left the confines of his [[Imperial Palace/Legends|palace]] on Coruscant, leaving a relative few military personnel ever actually seeing him face to face. As such, even though the various commanders merely carried out the orders issued by the Emperor, due to the stratocratic nature of the New Order, they held considerable practical control over the Empire.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" /> The next highest rank was that of the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], notably held by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. The individual who held this title had complete control over the Imperial Military, and answered only to the Emperor. In the absence of an official Emperor, the Supreme Commander often became the ''de-facto'' leader of the Empire, as was seen in the cases of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] and Gilad Pellaeon. This position was held by several different Imperial officials over the course of the Empire's history, including [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, Thrawn, and Gilad Pellaeon.

The Imperial Military was not only a physical superpower, but a mental one as well. [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader's stormtrooper division, the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], known as "Vader's Fist," inspired fear in any [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species. The infamous [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] were used by [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] to frighten the galaxy's citizens into submission. Despite the enormity of the Imperial war-machine, in many instances, its ability to wage campaigns of psychological terror proved more effective at suppressing the unending scores of denizens than actual displays of power. Much of the equipment used by the Empire was designed to enhance this effect, the fear-inspiring appearance of the [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]] being one example of this phenomena.

==History==
===Foundation===
{{Quote|Fear will keep the local systems in line&mdash;fear of this battlestation.|[[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin]], speaking of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
The Imperial Military formed as a realignment of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]]. Originally formed when then [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine was authorized to create a Galactic Military under his Emergency Powers, the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] was formed by clones from facilities on Kamino. These clones were created from the [[DNA/Legends|DNA]] of [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] under orders from [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]].

[[File:501st_Trooper_TBOH.png|thumb|right|250px|Though their armor changed, clones were still used as the primary fighting force of the Galactic Empire during its early years]]
Following the Clone Wars and the transformation from Republic to Empire, the clones were given new armor and weapons, and went from fighting droids to suppressing planetary uprisings on planets such as [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Palpatine used the lack of a surrender from the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] leaders to continue to build up his army and navy, although he was aware that they were all dead. During the early stages of the Empire's formation, the Imperial Military initially found innumerable recruits among various cadets of the Academy, which had been an elite educational and training institution with campuses throughout the known galaxy.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" /> Shortly into the Empire's infancy, however, a [[Ghost Prison incident|military coup]] was instigated by the first graduating class of the various Military branches, helmed by the then-Imperial Academy headmaster [[Gentis]], in order to end the Emperor's warmongering ways after stumbling upon the [[Imperial Crematorium]], which also led to Palpatine being temporarily poisoned with [[Aorth-6]].<ref name="Ghost Prison">''[[Star Wars: Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison]]''</ref> After the Kamino Uprising, Palpatine decided that having an entire army based on a single template was too dangerous, and began to diversify, although the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] remained composed of Fett clones. According to the [[New Order/Legends|New Order's]] ideology of human supremacy, the stormtroopers remained on the whole, human. Early conflicts for the Imperial Military included the [[Reconquest of the Rim]], which brought much of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] under Imperial control, and the [[Kwymar Suppressions/Legends|Kwymar Suppressions]].<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

===The Galactic Civil War===
{{Main|Galactic Civil War/Legends}}
[[File:ATATAssaultFormation-TCGtBoH.jpg|thumb|left|250px|AT-AT in attack formation during the Battle of Hoth]]
After facing a droid uprising on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] led by [[Gizor Dellso]], the biggest threat to the Imperial Military was the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. The two sides fought for years, in a [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|conflict spanning the entire galaxy]]. The three biggest battles were at [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Yavin]], [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], and [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Endor]]. At the time of the Battle of Yavin, the Imperial Military, according to Emperor Palpatine, was the largest fighting force in galactic history.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> Even though the Empire was victorious at Hoth, dealing a grievous blow to the Rebels, the Battles of Yavin and Endor resulted in major Alliance victories. In fact, Endor would see the end of the Emperor and his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|right hand man]], [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]],<ref name="kenner" /> sending the Imperial Military into chaos.

===Defeat and restoration===
[[File:ThrawnFleet.jpg|thumb|right|150px|The Imperial Military as it was led by Grand Admiral Thrawn]]
Following defeat at the hands of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Imperial Military split to follow multiple leaders, depending on their location and direct command. Several factions were led by officers and warlords such as [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]], [[Ysanne Isard]], and [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]. Though they all came close to defeating the New Republic, especially Thrawn, all ultimately failed. When Palpatine returned, much of the military sided with him. After his final defeat in [[Operation Shadow Hand]], they retreated to the portion of space known as [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Space]]. They would later reunite with the New Republic to fight the Yuuzhan Vong. After about [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], the Imperial Remnant began to regain power; after the [[Battle of Caamas]] in [[130 ABY]], it was once more the dominant faction in the galaxy. However, the Imperial Military was divided again when [[Roan Fel|Emperor Fel]] was forced out of power. Parts of the military remained loyal to him, and after its formation served the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]].

==Organization==
===Headquarters===
{{Quote|The Empire maintains order. People like you disrupt that order.|[[Sarkli]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Imperial_meeting_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A meeting of military officers.]]
The Imperial Military's [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|Commander-in-Chief]] was the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. However, the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] had direct control over the various Imperial forces. Another very high level organizational body was the [[Emperor's Advisory Committee on Military Affairs]], which advised the Emperor on military affairs at least up until the Battle of Yavin. In addition, its highest organizational body was the [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]], which oversaw the highest levels of the three primary branches of the Imperial Military: [[Naval Command (Imperial)|Naval Command]], [[Army Command]], and [[Stormtrooper Command/Legends|Stormtrooper Command]], alongside all support branches of the Imperial Military. High Command's role was to plan and coordinate the proper combination of [[Ground warfare/Legends|ground]], [[Starfighter combat/Legends|air]], [[Space warfare/Legends|space]], and [[Special forces/Legends|special operations]] forces to achieve the mission objective. High Command was also responsible for synchronizing military efforts with the [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]], [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]], the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]], and other intergovernmental partners.<ref name="Handbook" /> Although not actually part of Imperial High Command, the [[Battle Station Command/Legends|Battle Station Command]] was a similar high position that answered to Imperial High Command, and specifically headed the [[Battle Station Operations/Legends|Battle Station Operations]] branch, which was formed by Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin upon the completion of the Death Star.

===Administrative organization===
[[File:Handbook-Palpatineandofficers.png|thumb|right|250px|Galactic Emperor Palpatine and several Imperial officers]]
Imperial High Command had authority over three service branches and seven support divisions. The [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] was the Empire's spacefaring force and projected power through [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] such as the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]], and controlled the Empire's [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Fighters]] through the [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]]. The [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] was the Empire's planetary invasion and occupation force and controlled the Empire's [[Ground assault vehicle/Legends|armored vehicles]].<ref name="Warfare" /> The Army also controlled the [[Imperial Maritime Division]], which operated aquatic vehicles and submersibles on ocean planets and surface rivers.<ref name="Handbook" /> The [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]], the smallest of the branches, was the elite of the Imperial Military, fanatically loyal to the Emperor, and controlled the Empire's distinctive, [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|white-armored]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], and was responsible for first strikes, shock action, and ensuring the loyalty of crews aboard Navy ships.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

The seven support divisions of the Imperial Military were the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]], the [[Imperial Diplomatic Corps/Legends|Imperial Diplomatic Corps]], the [[Imperial Engineering Corps/Legends|Imperial Engineering Corps]], the [[Imperial Survey Corps/Legends|Imperial Survey Corps]], the [[Imperial Exploration Corps/Legends|Imperial Exploration Corps]], the [[Imperial Surgical Corps]], and the [[Imperial Military Police]]. IDMR was the military's research and development branch for new [[Warship/Legends|warships]], armaments and [[Battle station/Legends|battle stations]]. The Diplomatic Corps negotiated with hostile worlds with the aim of pacifying them without the use of force. The Engineering Corps was tasked with constructing strategic structures like garrisons, ore mines, power generators and space stations. The Exploration and Survey Corps was attached to the Imperial Navy and was used to expand the Empire's borders by finding new planets for conquest. The Surgical Corps was the Empire's medical branch and was also used to develop new [[Bioweapon/Legends|bioweapons]]. Finally, the Military Police ensured discipline in the ranks.<ref name="Handbook" />

Other branches of unspecified relationship to the main ten organizations were the [[Imperial Department of Munitions Resource Development]],<ref name="Planet of the Mists">''[[Planet of the Mists]]''</ref> [[Imperial Transport (organization)|Imperial Transport]],<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> the [[Internal Safeguards Division]],<ref name="Star Wars Sourcebook">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars Sourcebook Second Edition">[[The Star Wars Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Star Wars Sourcebook'' Second Edition]]</ref> the [[Imperial Biological Weapons Division]],<ref name="Death Troopers">''[[Death Troopers]]''</ref> the [[Imperial Palace Guard]],<ref name="Star Wars Adventure Journal 5">{{JournalCite|5|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> the [[Imperial Officer Corps/Legends|Imperial Officer Corps]],<ref name="Dark Forces">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref><ref name="Dark Forces II">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref> the [[Imperial Special Forces/Legends|Imperial Special Forces]],<ref name="The Mind Spider">[[Star Wars (1977) 63|''Star Wars'' (1977) 63]]</ref> an [[Unidentified Imperial program|indoctrination program]],<ref name="Dark Star">{{GalaxyCite|3|Lumiya: Dark Star of the Empire}}</ref> the [[Emperor's Demonstration Team]],<ref name="Endor Limited">{{CCG|set=Endor Limited|cardname=Corporal Misik}} {{1stm|{{CCG|set=Endor Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Grond}}}}</ref> the [[Imperial Demonstration Team]],<ref name="DSII Limited">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Captain Yorr}}</ref> and the [[Acolyte Program|Acolyte]] and [[Saber Program]]s.<ref name="The Force Unleashed II">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

Although technically not actual branches with the Imperial Military, the [[Department of Public Works]] and [[Department of System Exploration]] had several of its funds diverted at the behest of Emperor Palpatine to fund the development of the two Death Stars as well as the ''Eye of Palpatine'',<ref name="DSOTM">''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref> and top-secret research into starfighter development, several of which were done illegally. The Imperial Advisor [[Coh Veshiv]] uncovered the latter instance, although this ended up inadvertently outraging his liege due to a breach in security.<ref name="The Far Orbit Project">{{WEGCite|story=The Capture of Coh Veshiv|book=The Far Orbit Project}}</ref>

Although they are not actually part of the standard Imperial Military hierarchy, the [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] and [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] branches (acting as the intelligence gathering branch and [[secret police]] branch, respectively) nonetheless are important enough assets to various Imperial Military operations to allow them to work together with the Imperial Military, as their collected findings and work are vital for their various military operations, as well as to ensure the various branches are ideologically consistent.<ref name="Handbook" /> Similarly, while the [[Imperial Senate Guard/Legends|Imperial Senate Guards]] and [[Imperial Senate Sentinel]]s technically weren't part of the standard Imperial Military hierarchy due to being assigned for guard duty for matters related to the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], they nonetheless have sometimes been attached to and at times even commanded various Imperial Military units should the operation be important enough to require their presence.<ref name="The Force Unleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> The [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order (COMPNOR)]], similar to the ISB, was not actually part of the standard Imperial Military hierarchy, but it often was attached to it for largely the same reasons as the ISB (which had itself been a creation of COMPNOR), with the inclusion of [[CompForce/Legends|CompForce]], the military wing of COMPNOR, as an [[COMPNOR Regiment|actual regiment]] in the Imperial Military.<ref name="Handbook" /> Likewise, while not actually part of the Imperial Military, the [[Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations/Legends|Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations]], and by extension its units the [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Rangers]] and [[Special Enforcement Officer/Legends|Special Enforcement Officers]], sometimes worked with the Imperial Military if any criminal investigations happened to involve both parties, as the former had jurisdiction throughout most of the known galaxy.

The Imperial Military was governed by various regulations. Imperial Military personnel followed and were disciplined under the [[Imperial Military Code]]. One regulation required all Imperial vessels to release garbage into the vacuum of space before making a hyperspace jump.<ref name="Episode V">{{Film|V}}</ref> Another was that, the moment when an executive vessel (such as a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]]) had lowered its ramp, all personnel within the docking area were to stand at attention.<ref name="DSOTM" /> One specific set of codes was Section 12-C, which defined capital offenses, which included but was not limited to incitement to mutiny, participation in mutiny, concealing mutineers or evidence of mutiny or planned mutiny and concealing saboteurs or evidence of sabotage or planned sabotage.<ref name="Children of the Jedi">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>

Although technically not part of the Imperial Military, [[Privateer/Legends|Privateers]] have an unofficial relationship with the Imperial Military, often raiding enemy shipping under Emperor Palpatine's explicit permission via a letter of marque, with the Imperial Military tolerating their presence in the Outer Rim and letting them have free reign as long as it didn't interfere with their own affairs.<ref name="Handbook" />

===Tactical organization===
The Empire's strategy was described in the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]] promulgated by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] of the [[Oversector Outer]]. Under the Tarkin Doctrine, the Empire's main operational theaters were the [[Oversector/Legends|Oversectors]], which consolidated hundreds of smaller [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] to enable military operations without the interference of political borders.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

Individual sectors were controlled by [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] and the Oversectors by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]], politico-military [[Governor/Legends|governors]] with control over all military assets in their sector. The original twenty [[Sector Army/Legends|sector armies]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] expanded dramatically until the Imperial Army composed of thousands of [[Sector army|sector armies]] and the Navy over a thousand [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Groups]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

In addition, ambition for the highest posts was encouraged amongst officers to keep competition fierce (with the penalty for failure being death), which likewise meant that a significant number of the Empire's commanders within the New Order being those of formidable military talents, owing to the New Order's valuing ruthless efficiency. However, in some cases, due to bureaucracy and political whims, incapable men were promoted to high posts.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" />

==Personnel==
===Specializations===
[[File:Snowtrooper_Captain.jpg|thumb|left|An Imperial [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtrooper]] captain]]
Under the Imperial Military's [[Non-huMan]] rule, members of the Imperial Military were almost invariably [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. Official Imperial policy regarded most [[Alien/Legends|alien]] species as being unfit for command or even self-determination.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" /> Through relentless government [[Propaganda/Legends|propaganda]], Imperial citizens were led to believe that this composition stemmed from practical concerns, such as the need for standardized control surfaces, cockpits, and other equipment. In reality, however, the policy was rooted in Emperor Palpatine’s deep-seated contempt for non-Human species.<ref name="Rebellion Era Campaign Guide">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

The few alien or female military personnel, such as [[Bertroff Hissa]], [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]], or [[Natasi Daala]] rose to high rank through concealing their backgrounds, obtaining powerful patrons, or through raw skill alone.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

The Empire used many foot soldiers in battle. The [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] were the backbone of the Imperial military, serving as the Empire's shock troops, much like many of them did as [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Some stormtroopers were clones left from the Clone Wars, but [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] decided to start cloning other soldiers from different men and start non-clone recruitment after the [[Kamino uprising|Kamino Uprising]]. There were also specialized versions, such as [[Dark Trooper/Legends|Dark troopers]] and [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtroopers]], that were tasked with specific goals as well as to work in specific environments. Other specializations included the [[Vehicle Command Crewer|Army Pilots]] who drove the Empire's [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and armored vehicles, the [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Imperial Army troopers]] who were by far the most common soldiers in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the Navy's [[Imperial gunner/Legends|Gunners]], the [[TIE pilot]]s of the [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]], [[Imperial Marines/Legends|Imperial Marines]], specialized stormtroopers trained for shipboard fighting, and the [[zero-G assault stormtrooper]]s trained for combat in the vacuum of space.

[[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] held command appointments over ships, troops and military units. Such men tended to be [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlders]], and lack of powerful connections within the military hierarchy could be a bar to high rank. Officers tended to be highly [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] and fully supportive of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order's]] anti-alien policies.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" />

[[File:Lord-vaders-persuasion.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Lord Vader leads Imperial forces]]
As [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]],<ref name="kenner" /> [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader was one of the uppermost figures of the Imperial Military, with authority second only to that of Emperor Palpatine.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook2">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> The other senior officers were the twelve [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]], a cadre of naval strategists, researchers, and [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] partisans appointed in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] by the Emperor himself. Called the "Circle of Twelve" by Palpatine, they were assembled to be a leadership cadre for the entire Imperial Military.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

[[Missile launcher trooper|Imperial Missile Launcher Troopers]] and [[Missile launcher trooper|Imperial Armored Missile Troopers]] played the role of anti-air infantry during various ground operations.<ref name="Galactic Battlegrounds">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> In addition, at least until [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], the military also had [[Saber Guard]]s and [[Imperial Sith Acolyte]]s, which were trained force-sensitive warriors dedicated to lightsaber combat and force abilities, respectively, for use against force users.<ref name="The Force Unleashed II" />

===Training===
{{Main|Imperial Academy/Legends}}
[[File:Imperial_training_academy.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Recruits train at the Imperial Naval Academy]]
The Imperial Military took over the ancient system of academies that had trained personnel of the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], [[Planetary Security Forces]], and [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] for millennia. Navy recruits attended [[Sector Naval Academy|Sector Naval Academies]], and the most promising graduates could be selected for advanced training at the [[Imperial Naval Academy/Legends|Imperial Naval Academy]] on [[Prefsbelt IV/Legends|Prefsbelt IV]] or the [[Republic Navy War College/Legends|Navy War College]] on [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]]. [[Imperial Army Officer Training Academy|Army Officer Training Academies]] similarly took in prospective soldiers, and the best [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]] might be assigned to the prestigious [[Raithal Academy/Legends|Raithal Academy]] or the [[Corulag Academy]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" /> The first graduates of the Academy, however, were infamous for instigating a military coup against Palpatine to end the latter's warmongering ways.<ref name="Ghost Prison" />

[[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtrooper]] training took place at the [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]] which used the planet's high gravity to build tougher, more resilient troopers. Training for [[TIE pilot]]s took place subsequently to basic training for Naval personnel at a [[Flight school/Legends|flight school]], typically aboard a [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

===Ranks===
{{Main|Rank insignia plaque/Legends}}
[[File:Imperial_Officer_IACS.png|thumb|right|200px|An Imperial officer with the rank of Lieutenant]]
Officer ranks within the Imperial Military was denoted by a specific combination of colored squares and [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] worn on the uniform.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" /> The Military divided rank into ''Position'', ''Line rank'', and ''Specialist rank''. ''Position'' referred to an officer's current assignment on a ship or unit as opposed to permanent rank, and included the honorary titles of [[High Admiral]] and [[Warlord of the Empire]], usually granted to [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]], [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]] and [[Grand General/Legends|Grand Generals]].<ref name="Warfare" /> Other titles included [[Baron of the Empire/Legends|Baron of the Empire]] and [[Tan (title)|Tan]]. Ironically, the title of Warlord of the Empire would later become infamous for the splintering of the Empire post-Endor, where various rogue Imperial officers created fiefdoms that feuded with each other, to the extent that they were referred to as [[Warlord/Legends|Warlords]].<ref name="Imperial Warlords">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-1|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>

''Line ranks'' were permanent ranks held by those who commanded ships, military units, or fleets. There were very few officers with permanent line ranks above that of Navy [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]] or Army [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]].<ref name="Warfare" />

''Specialist rank'' was held by those in the technical branches and broadly mirrored the line ranks of the Imperial Army. Specialists promoted above the rank of [[General/Legends|General]] would be promoted into the line ranks but would receive honorary titles related to their branch.<ref name="Warfare" />

==Equipment==
===Uniforms===
{{Main|Imperial military uniforms/Legends}}
[[File:E-11sandDLT-19sinuse-Empire18.png|thumb|left|300px|Imperials in tunic attire and stormtroopers fight in trench warfare on Maridun.]]
Officers in the Army and Navy wore an olive-gray uniform tunic and trousers with matching caps and black leather boots. Officers in the Stormtrooper Corps wore identical uniforms but all-black in color, and in battle wore the same [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|white armor]] as their soldiers but with rank insignia. Similar black-colored NCO uniforms were also prevalent among veteran pilots and prison guards.

Enlisted personnel wore a variety of coveralls or [[Jumpsuit/Legends|jumpsuits]] depending on role. [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Imperial Army troopers]] wore gray battledress with partial body armor and helmets in combat. [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Imperial Navy troopers]] wore black jumpsuits and large helmets, while [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] and [[Specialist/Legends|specialists]] wore gray jumpsuits with black caps.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

The most striking military uniforms were the [[Grand Admiral's uniform/Legends|stark white uniforms]] of the twelve [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]], which also bore gold epaulettes to show the seniority of their rank.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Handbook" />

Around [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], various Imperial officers had their hair cut in a way that exposed the sideburns, although this practice was discontinued some time after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="ANH" />

Although technically not a standard uniform for the Imperial Military, various Imperials stationed at [[Restuss]] utilized the [[Crusader Mark III armor]] provided to them by Black Sun during the [[Battle of Restuss|battle]] against Rebel forces for the [[Star Core]]. The Rebels, likewise, wore [[Crusader Mark II armor]] during that time, and also developed by Black Sun as a way of profiting from the war by selling [[Crusader armor]] to both sides without tipping either side off.<ref name="It's Not My War">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66907&resource=features|text=''It's Not My War!''}}</ref>

===Ground Vehicles===
[[File:AT-ST-SWGTCGart.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Walker/Legends|Walkers]] were the critical component of the Imperial Ground Forces.]]
Walkers such as [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-STs]] and [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-ATs]] symbolized the might and resources of the Empire. They were giant weapons of war, feared by all. Many believed such weapons to be invincible. However, the AT- AT had two fatal flaws&mdash;its neck and its legs. (Rebel Snowspeeder pilots exploited these weaknesses on Hoth.) After the formation of the Empire at the end of the Clone Wars, many vehicles left over from that previous galactic conflict were used by the military, along with Separatist light vehicles, such as the [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|Dwarf Spider Droid]]. Later on in the Empire's existence as the primary galactic power, older vehicles, such as the AT-AP, Juggernaut, and cargo AT-TEs were used in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].

Less widely known vehicles included the [[All Terrain Recon Transport/Legends|AT-RT]], [[All Terrain Anti Aircraft/Legends|AT-AA]], [[All Terrain Attack Pod/Legends|AT-AP]], [[All Terrain Personal Transport/Legends|AT-PT]], [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]], [[Mountain Terrain Armored Transport|MT-AT]], [[HAVw A6 Juggernaut/Legends|HAVw A6 Juggernauts]] and the [[TX-130T fighter tank]]. These units were not as famous as their counterparts but remained very dangerous to enemy units.

===Ships===
[[File:Strang_Conqueror.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Admiral [[Victor Strang]] with his [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]]-equipped Star Destroyer, [[Conqueror (superlaser)|''Conqueror'']]]]
Although [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]] had served valiantly in the defense of the Republic during the Clone Wars, the rise of the Galactic Empire quickly turned the powerful vessels into symbols of fear and intimidation. The ''Venator'' and [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyers]] were stripped of their Republic markings and became the first of many warships that would comprise the Imperial Starfleet. Despite the total collapse of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, the Empire's military spending would only increase, leading to the development of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]]. Eventually, the former Republic vessels would be phased out in favor of the new ''Imperial'' class, which would become the primary symbol of Imperial space power.

The [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruiser]], also known as the ''Interdictor''-class heavy cruiser, ''Interdictor''-class Star Destroyer, or ''Interdictor''-class medium frigate, was a 600-meter-long cruiser built on the standard Vindicator-class heavy cruiser hull. This vessel was equipped with 4 [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projectors]], massive devices that projected pseudo-gravity that could prevent a vessel from escaping into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. The New Republic captured the remaining Immobilizer 418s, and upgraded their gravity- well projectors.

The Empire used many capital ships as frigates. Some of the most common were the [[Victory II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Victory II-class Star Destroyer]] and the [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class light cruiser]]. They varied in size and power, but each was still a force to be reckoned with. They were more specialized than Star Destroyers, and though Star Destroyers were the backbone of the Fleet, frigates were more commonly used, unless a major battle was at hand.
The culmination of the Star Destroyer design came in the form of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]], which was larger and more powerful still. Several ''Executor''-class ships were known to have been constructed, including the original [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], the ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'', the [[Iron Fist (Executor-class)|''Iron Fist'']] and one other Super Star Destroyer of unidentified class which served much later on fighting against the Yuuzhan Vong.

The fleet also used two [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class Super Star Destroyers]] during [[Operation Shadow Hand]]. These mighty ships were equipped with superlasers powerful enough to melt a planet's crust.

===Starfighters===
{{Main|TIE series/Legends}}
[[File:TIEs_SoG.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A TIE fighter formation]]
The Empire had millions of [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], coming in many varieties. All varieties of the TIE (except for the TIE Defender, TIE Hunter, TIE Avenger, TIE Phantom, and the TIE Advanced X1), however, lacked shields. This made the craft more vulnerable than the other ships used in the Imperial Military, forcing the [[TIE pilot|pilots]] to fly with greater precision, demanding the highest skill from each one.

The [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] was the Empire's most common fighter. Though the fighter had no shields, it was very fast, and, most important to Palpatine, it was cheap. There were many variations on the original, such as the [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE Interceptor]], the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE Bomber]], and the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE Defender]]. With the exception of the Defender, all were relatively cheap and extremely efficient.

The Imperial R.O.E. (Rules Of Engagement) stated that Imperial TIE Fighters must have a 3 to 1 ratio advantage over enemy fighters in order to engage. Beating the enemy in numbers was a key part of Imperial strategy.

==Behind the scenes==
In [[A. C. Crispin]]'s book, ''[[The Paradise Snare]]'', it is subtly hinted that [[The Imperial March]] is "the martial theme of the Imperial Navy."

''[[Death Star Designer]]'' provides a few information on the color symbolism in the Imperial military. It says "no one is ever fired or telekinetically executed for choosing Imperial Grey. It's the traditional color for imperial ships and stations". It also talks about "Sith Black", which "adds a touch of ancient dread to any battle station". "Stormtrooper White" is said to be "the perfect choice for the battlestation designer that knows that what we don't see is more terrifying than what we do". Finally, "Republic Red" follows the teaching of "co-opting the legacy of republican traditions".
